email_en:
Subject: Exhibitor Application Inquiry — GEGYjiji

Dear Tokyo Art Book Fair team,

TABF's reputation for bringing together independently published art books and zines with a genuine curatorial sensibility is what draws me to reach out about exhibiting at a future edition. I am GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and since 2020 I have maintained a daily watercolor practice — a series called "diary" — that grew into my first solo illustration collection, Colour Diary, published in October 2021. My work moves through the ordinary: red walls and alleyways, pools and green ponds, the warmth of sunlight in a familiar street — scenes that are entirely everyday and, I hope, quietly moving. You can find my work on Instagram at @gegyjiji. I would be grateful to learn more about the exhibitor application process, including deadlines, booth formats, and any fees, for the next edition.

GEGYjiji

name: UTRECHT
email_en:
Subject: Inquiry from illustrator GEGYjiji — watercolor zine / consignment possibility

Dear UTRECHT team,

I have long admired how UTRECHT brings together artist books, zines, and illustrated works that sit quietly between fine art and everyday life, and I think my work may belong in that same conversation. I am GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and in 2021 I published Colour Diary, a small illustration collection grown from a daily watercolor practice that documents domestic interiors, neighborhood light, and the quiet texture of city life — much of it observed here in Tokyo. My work has been shown in Tokyo most recently as part of Tide from China, a group exhibition at ACG_Labo in Harajuku in 2023, and I am now looking to place printed work or original pieces in spaces where that kind of attentive, intimate scale feels at home. I would love to explore whether a consignment arrangement or a small exhibition might be a possibility, and you are welcome to see more of my work on Instagram at @gegyjiji. Thank you very much for your time, and I hope to hear from you.

GEGYjiji
email_ja:
件名: 水彩イラスト集『Colour Diary』のお取り扱いについてのご相談

UTRECHTご担当者様

UTRECHTさんが扱われるアーティストブックやZINEの選書を拝見し、日常のなかに宿る美しさを丁寧にすくいとった作品たちが並ぶ空間に、自分の本を置いていただけないかと思いご連絡いたしました。私はGEGYjiji（ジェジー）と申します。中国・湖南省出身、現在は東京を拠点に活動している水彩イラストレーターです。2020年から毎日水彩画を描き続けており、赤い壁、路地、プール、緑の池といったごく普通の日常の景色を、心に残る一枚へと変えていくこの「diary」という実践から、2021年10月に初のイラスト集『Colour Diary』が生まれました。作品はInstagram（@gegyjiji）でもご覧いただけます。UTRECHTさんの棚に並ぶ本の一冊として、この小さな日々の記録をお届けできればと思い、お取り扱いやご相談の機会をいただけますと大変嬉しく存じます。

どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。

GEGYjiji

Dear B&B Shimokitazawa team,

With warm regards,
GEGYjiji

GEGYjiji

Subject: Application for START Box Studio Space — GEGYjiji (Watercolor Illustrator)

Dear START Box ササハタハツ / 白鬚 Team,

I am writing to apply for studio space through the 2026年度利用者募集 program, drawn to START Box's commitment to supporting emerging artists working at the intersection of daily practice and place-based observation. My name is GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor illustrator based in Tokyo, and my work — including my first illustration collection Colour Diary, which grew from a daily watercolor diary practice I have maintained since 2020 — focuses on the quiet atmospheres of Tokyo neighborhoods, domestic interiors, and the particular quality of urban light as seen through a cross-cultural lens. In February 2023, I participated in the group exhibition Tide from China Part1 at ACG_Labo in Harajuku, my first exhibition in Japan, alongside five other Chinese illustrators. I believe dedicated studio space within a community rooted in Tokyo's local art ecology would meaningfully support the next phase of my practice, particularly as I develop new work and exhibition relationships in the city. A portfolio of my watercolor illustration work is available on Instagram at @gegyjiji, and I would welcome the opportunity to share further materials or speak with your team at your convenience.

GEGYjiji

Sincerely,
GEGYjiji

GEGYjiji

Subject: Consignment inquiry — Colour Diary (illustration collection) by GEGYjiji

Dear COW BOOKS team,

I admire how carefully your Nakameguro shop is curated — the sense that every book on the shelf has been chosen by someone who actually reads, which is rare and matters to me as both a reader and an artist. I am GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor illustrator based in Tokyo, and I would love to ask whether you might consider stocking my first illustration collection, Colour Diary (色彩日記), a small-format book that grew out of a daily watercolor diary practice I began in 2020. The work focuses on quiet Tokyo interiors, neighborhood light, cats, and the particular way a city looks when you are still learning to belong to it — themes I think might sit naturally alongside the books you already carry. You can see my recent work on Instagram at @gegyjiji, and I am happy to bring a copy of the book in person if a visit would be easier than corresponding by email. Thank you sincerely for your time, and I hope to hear from you.

GEGYjiji

Subject: Open Call Submission — GEGYjiji (Watercolor / Tokyo-based)

Dear ARRIVAL Team,

I came across your Osaka open call and was drawn to the structured, curated approach ARRIVAL takes to introducing artists — it feels like a considered context for work that asks the viewer to slow down. I am GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and my practice centers on the utterly ordinary: red walls, alleyways, pools, green ponds, the particular quality of light in a familiar street corner — scenes most people walk past, which I try to make into something moving. This work grew into my first solo illustration collection, Colour Diary, published in October 2021, and continues through an ongoing daily watercolor series I have kept since 2020. A fuller picture of the work is on Instagram at @gegyjiji. I would be glad to share image files, a statement, or any additional materials your selection process requires — please let me know what the submission asks for and I will send everything promptly.

GEGYjiji

Subject: Exhibitor Inquiry — GEGYjiji, Watercolor / Tokyo Gendai 2026

Dear Tokyo Gendai Team,

I am writing to ask about the process for individual artists or small exhibitors to participate in Tokyo Gendai 2026, as I understand gallery applications are currently open for the September edition. I am GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and my work finds its subjects in the ordinary — red walls, alleyways, pools, the light in a familiar park — and tries to make those scenes feel like somewhere the viewer half-remembers. My first solo illustration collection, Colour Diary, grew directly from a daily watercolor practice I have maintained since 2020, and I made my first Tokyo exhibition as part of the group show Tide from China Part1 at ACG_Labo in Harajuku in 2023. My work can be seen on Instagram at @gegyjiji. I would be grateful for any information on how independent artists may apply, and whether the format of the fair accommodates smaller presentations.

Thank you for your time.

GEGYjiji
